name: Daylio
one_liner: Mood and activity tracker: tap an icon for how you feel and what you did, then see which activities go with better or worse days.
best_for: People who want a quick daily mood log without much writing
People in therapy who want mood and activity data to review with a clinician
People who want their diary kept on their phone without an account
not_for: Anyone in crisis or thinking about suicide: call or text 988
People looking for treatment, therapy or guided exercises
People who need clinician-facing monitoring (reports have to be exported and shared by hand)
short_description: Icon-based mood and activity diary that shows patterns over time. Entries stay on your phone; no account needed.
long_description: Daylio is a mood diary from Relaxio s.r.o. Each entry is a mood rating plus taps on activity icons (sleep, exercise, work, people and so on), with an optional written note. The app turns these into calendars, mood charts and simple activity-mood links, and can export PDF or CSV reports. There is no account: the developer says entries are stored only on your device, with optional backups to your own Google Drive or iCloud that it cannot access. The free version stays unlimited for basic logging; Premium adds more statistics and customization. It is a self-monitoring tool, not treatment, and we found no published study of its effect on mood.
patient_summary: You pick a mood face and tap icons for what you did that day, with an optional note; it takes under a minute. Over time Daylio shows your mood trends and which activities go with good or bad days, and you can export a PDF or CSV to bring to a therapist. The basic app is free; Premium is a paid upgrade.

pricing.notes: The free version stays unlimited for basic mood and activity logging. Premium adds advanced statistics, more customization and extra backup options, with a 7-day free trial. Premium prices are from a July 2026 review and may vary by region and sale; check the in-app price.

privacy.notes: Policy (read 2026-10-27) says entries stay on your device with no account, and Apple Health data is never shared with advertisers, but it uses Google Advertising ID (with permission) to measure its ads and never says whether it sells or shares other data for advertising.

seo.title: Daylio: Simple Mood Tracker App | HeyPsych
seo.meta_description: Daylio is a mood tracking journal app that uses icons instead of writing, making it easy to track emotions, activities, and mental health patterns.

faqs.q: How does Daylio mood tracking work?
faqs.a: Each day, select your mood level (great to awful) and tag activities you did. Daylio requires no writing—just tapping icons. Over time, the app shows patterns and correlations between activities and moods.
Basic mood tracking is free. Premium ($2.99/month or $35.99/year) adds unlimited entries per day, advanced statistics, automatic backups, and no ads. The free version works well for basic tracking.

faqs.q: Can I share Daylio data with my therapist?
faqs.a: Yes, Daylio allows exporting data as PDF or CSV files. Many people share mood reports with therapists to identify patterns and track progress between sessions.

Daylio shows which activities correlate with better or worse moods, mood trends over weeks/months, day-of-week patterns, and how consistent your mood tracking is. These insights help identify what supports your mental health.

primary_uses: Seeing mood trends and activity-mood links
Exporting PDF or CSV reports to share with a clinician

how_clinicians_use_it: Assign as homework for patients to track mood between sessions
Have patients export reports to review together in session
Help patients identify activity-mood patterns to target in treatment
Monitor treatment progress through mood trends over time
clinician.implementation_notes: No clinician dashboard - patient shares exports manually. PDF and CSV export available. Consider for patients who find journaling overwhelming.
